transcript.text: ...rat, with a single that's just been released in the States on a 12-inch, and it's called Lay It Down.
10 minutes past 10, the Friday Rock Show, BBC Radio 1, how's your luck?
Giovanni Rossi-Comistai, he lives out there in Bradford, West Yorkshire, and he sent me this little clipping from a local newspaper.
The newspaper is actually the Telegraph and Argus.
It says Radio 1, talking about programmes here on a Friday. Radio 1, 5.30 newsbeat, 5.40 roundtable.
7, Andy Peebles, 10 to 12, the Friday Rock Shock.
Exactly what every grandmother in the country is saying.
Communication here from Dee Fulford of somewhere.
Dee Fulford says, could you please say a big I OPE to all the KISS fans and freaks and maniacs
that went to see them on their best ever yet animalized tour.
Especially everybody went to see them at Leeds.
My last request, could you tell that hairy fellow that I know by the name of Borgly,
I think it's B-A-W, B-A-G-W-E, can't read the writing.
Borgly, boogly, boogly, whatever.
Get your haircut before you lose himself in all of it.
If you want to look like Paul Stanley, then you'd better cut a few feet off.
This is Lion Rampant.
You're only a child is the cry of the wild.
A repeat session by them tonight.
Before that, you heard Lion Rampant and their first number.
It was called Time Again.
Here's a letter.
It's quite straightforward in the beginning, but it gets very sad.
It's from Pete Hall of Shipnall.
I think it is in Shropshire.
It says, Dear TV, I'm writing this letter whilst listening to your
Absolutely superb show.
Though there are one or two complaints I have to make.
I've been listening to your show for quite a while now,
and I've heard only one Saxon, which was Dallas 1pm,
and only one MSG record,
which was such a long time ago now I've forgotten what it was.
Please, will you act quickly? Do something about it.
Also, could you play a request, which is for my brother?
Now this is where it gets sad.
Something really heavy would be appropriate,
as he's going weird and listening to Bronski beat and Howard Jones.
My brother is called Mike
He lives in Whitchurch
He ought to be thrown in the bay
Favourite albums of all time
I say I think
I've only heard it twice in its entirety
I'm going to listen to it again tonight
It's a drive home in the motor car
And if I get home before the album finishes
I'm going to sit outside the house and listen to it
Marillion, from the album Misplaced Childhood
The track you heard there was called Blind Curve
There is a pretty strong chance
That Fish of Marillion will be live
On Into The Music next Thursday
About 95% secure he was last night.
If he is, well, certainly would be a pleasure to have him in the studio.
He's a great chatter, so a very sort of straightforward character as well.
I thought it would be a nice idea if you have any questions you'd like me to put to Fish,
if he turns up, if he can turn up,
jot them down on the back of a postcard, back of an envelope, anything you like really,
and send them to Fish, into the music,
that's the name of the Thursday night programme, just in case you don't know it,
into the music rather,
BBC Radio 1, London, W1A4, WW.
OK, fish.
Into the music, BBC Radio 1, London, W1A4, WW.
And if he can't make it next Thursday,
well, ultimately, I'm sure he will.
This fella here who's in the 1st Battalion,
the Scots Guards,
at Elizabeth Barracks, Purbright and Surrey,
Costa del Purbright.
Guardsman T. Laird.
That's town, there.
Dear Thomas, he says,
do us a big favour,
say a very big hello to my doll.
Back home.
Her name is Sharon Scott.
She's from Easterhus in Glasgow.
Sharon Scott, how are you?
Also tell a piece that I love her very, very much, and I am missing her a lot.
Also mention my mates, Eddie and Big Joe and Gibby, or maybe Jibby,
and all the heavy headcases that know me.
Right, mate.
Pam Laird, 1st Battalion, Scott's Guards.
I know some mates of yours are in the 2nd Battalion, Scott's Guards, in Cyprus.
Exactly 10.30.
This should have gone out of the programme last night, but last night's programme is not a request show.
I'll do it tonight.
I would imagine they've probably got better things to do.
Greg Skite, S-K-Y-T-E
at Barwell in Leicester
wrote me this letter.
I'd be very grateful if you dedicate any record
on your Thursday programme to my wife
Karen on our wedding day,
which was actually yesterday.
We will be married at Hartsdale Church, Nuneaton.
Please tell her I love her one heck of a lot.
Well, Greg, if you are listening,
Greg and Karen, lots of luck to you.
And happy life, continually.
This is a man called Trash.
They are a pet hate.
That's a track by them from our repeat session by them.
I love listening to their words. Good lyricist.
Out of that band, the track was called Love Me Madly.
It's exactly 20 minutes to 11.
Before that, you heard the American band.
At least I think they're American.
I hope I'm right there.
A band called Trash from an album called Burning Rock.
The track was Rock Me, Rock You.
Friday Rock Show next week between 10 o'clock and midnight is going to come to you live.
